entities.evidence: The flood narrative identifies this Noah as Lamech’s son, the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth, matching the source tag.
The name יַהְוֶה identifies the God in whose eyes Noah found favor. The source tag LORD refers to the same bearer as the earlier Yahweh proposal.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the subject of מָצָא חֵן, “found favor.” The verse names Noah as the one who found favor in Yahweh’s eyes.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed conjunction וְ, here “but.”

analysis.evidence: נֹחַ is the subject and חֵן ‘favor’ is the direct object. With בְּעֵינֵי יַהְוֶה, the clause reads ‘Noah found favor in the eyes of YHWH.’
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: Noah is the subject of מָצָא, and חֵן is its direct object. The phrase בְּעֵינֵי יַהְוֶה identifies whose favour Noah found: “Noah found favour in the eyes of Yahweh.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי יַהְוֶה, Noah finds favor, and יַהְוֶה completes the construct phrase עֵינֵי יַהְוֶה. The phrase identifies whose favorable regard Noah enjoys.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ + common noun עֵינֵי, dual construct, common gender.
analysis.sense: in the eyes of: in one's judgment, regard

analysis.evidence: In בְּעֵינֵי יַהְוֶה, “in the eyes of Yahweh,” the name completes the construct phrase and identifies the one in whose eyes Noah found favor.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel
